members.title: Highrider liaison
members.bio:
A recent arrival at the People's Center, Kerubo represents a new connection between the RSC and their Highrider allies. She carries herself with the distinctive bearing of the space-born - precise movements and careful observation that comes from living where small mistakes can be fatal.

Like many of her generation who grew up in the post-independence Highrider Confederation, Kerubo combines technical expertise with strong cultural ties to African traditions. Her family's connections to Pan-African revolutionary movements provide personal context for understanding the RSC's work, though she keeps details of these connections private.

At the Center, she works closely with Iō to understand RSC operations, particularly their martial arts programs. Her interest in ground-based combat techniques reflects both personal passion and professional necessity - operating in Earth gravity requires different approaches than orbital close combat. Those who train with her note how she analyzes movements with the methodical attention characteristic of Highrider culture.

While her exact role continues to develop, she maintains the careful diplomatic neutrality typical of Highrider representatives. She builds connections deliberately, particularly with the RSC's security personnel, while maintaining clear boundaries between her duties to the Confederation and her involvement with the organization. Her presence in the Wuguan has become increasingly common, where she both learns and offers perspectives from her own martial traditions.

Those seeking to understand her mission might note how the Highriders' own revolutionary history - from colonial workforce to independent power - mirrors aspects of what the RSC hopes to achieve. For now though, she remains an observer and student.

members.title: Community Kitchen · Original cadre
members.bio:
Chan-Woo Park spent his early nights in Night City's street racing scene. He was good behind the wheel - not legendary, but reliable enough to make decent money and earn respect without drawing too much attention. During the day, he worked at a Triad-aligned auto shop in Little China, learning the mechanical skills that would later prove valuable while staying clear of the outfit's shadier operations.

His parents had come to Night City as refugees from the Second Korean War. Like many immigrants, they found themselves trapped in Little China's underground economy - his mother in textile work, his father eventually turning to Black Lace to cope with the endless grind. Park used his racing earnings to help keep the family afloat, but watching his father's spiral left marks that would shape his later path.

The family's connection to Iō began at the original Comrade Clinic, where his father sought treatment for his addiction. During the long hours spent in the clinic's waiting room, Park and Iō discovered shared ground in unexpected places - lengthy discussions about old Japanese anime between appointments, debates about eastern religions, quiet conversations about family obligations. When his father's treatment succeeded where others had failed, Park started volunteering at the clinic, initially just helping with maintenance and deliveries.

When Iō proposed establishing the first People's Center, Park brought practical skills honed by necessity. The same attention to detail that kept racing engines running now went into stretching kitchen resources and maintaining the Center's resources. His old Lada, perpetually in various states of repair, became a familiar sight throughout South Night City's back alleys.

These days, Park runs the People's Center's kitchen with the same quiet efficiency he once applied to engine work. He's developed a knack for turning limited supplies into meals that keep both spirits and bodies going. The kitchen doubles as an unofficial meeting spot after hours, where residents often find him working late, usually willing to share both food and measured advice.

Despite being one of the original six cadres who helped establish the RSC, Park maintains a low profile. He takes his turns on security detail without complaint, handles logistics runs when needed, and helps train new members in both driving and basic combat skills. His old connections in Little China occasionally prove useful, though he's careful to maintain boundaries with his former Triad employers.

Those who work closely with him note his methodical nature extends beyond just cooking and mechanics. He maintains the Center's vehicles with ritualistic precision, keeps careful inventory of kitchen supplies, and approaches combat training with the same patient attention to detail. Few know about his serious Elflines Online habit - a rare indulgence he keeps carefully separate from his public persona.

Park spends his off hours visiting his parents in Little China or occasionally checking in on old contacts from the racing scene. His father's ongoing recovery remains a priority, though these days their conversations are as likely to be about Park's latest kitchen experiments as about treatment. He's been quietly working on a recipe book, combining his mother's Korean cooking with ingredients available in the Combat Zone - though he tends to deflect when asked about it.

The most common sight of Park remains in the Center's kitchen during meal times, carefully plating food while keeping an eye on supplies, staff, and the steady stream of residents who've come to rely on both his cooking and his quiet presence.

members.title: Security · Gardener liaison · Original cadre
members.bio:
Arina Morozova arrived in Night City at eighteen with nothing but a Moscow education, sambo training, and the knowledge that no one would ever fight for her.

She'd spent her childhood learning to read rooms. First in the unstable apartments of her mother Zoya's rotating relationships, then in the wealthy household of Viktor Morozov, the Zhirafa executive who married her mother when Arina was eight. For one year, Viktor felt like a father. Then Zoya got pregnant, and Arina became furniture. She spent the next eight years as auxiliary parent to her half-siblings Vera and Misha while watching Viktor's attention go entirely to his biological children. She tried everything to win it back. Perfect marks, competitive sambo, the flawless elegance Moscow society demanded. It didn't work. She was auditioning for a role she'd already lost.

When Viktor found someone new, he kept his children and disposed of the rest. Zoya negotiated for money, not for her daughter. Arina watched her mother calculate, adapt, survive. But she did not fight. The flight to Night City taught her the final lesson: she would survive some way that didn't depend on anyone else.

Four years at the Slammer followed. She started behind the bar, moved to running books on the cinder block arena fights, and eventually found the real money: provoking unofficial matches with carefully chosen words. She learned which egos to prod, which grudges to stoke, which fights would pay out. Fixer-adjacent work put her in dangerous rooms and taught her how violence operated professionally. It also got her in a few fights of her own.

When she'd saved enough, she built something clean: a corner store in Little Europe selling Gardener produce. For four years, it worked. Then Continental Brands came with price wars, supply strangulation, and hit squads against the Gardeners she'd partnered with. They didn't burn her bodega. They just made it impossible to operate.

She saw Iō and Sherwood hit the Oasis shortly after. While others celebrated, she watched with mounting frustration. One burning storefront was theater. She burst into the People's Center the next day, armed and angry, demanding they organize another strike. She wanted to burn every Oasis in Little Europe to the ground. Iō bet her she couldn't last a week seeing how they actually intended to operate. One week became years.

As one of the original six cadre, Arina trained under Iō and Le Fou and later Sorry and Luthiel and still serves on their security work gang. Her real value emerged in building relationships. Particularly with the Gardeners, where her understanding of small margins and supply chains (learned the hard way) makes her invaluable. She's the informal liaison, the one who speaks their language because her bodega once needed the same things they need.

Her family situation is complicated. Viktor transferred to Night City years after casting her out; Vera and Misha now live in the Executive Zone as privileged youth, and Arina maintains contact in neutral territory. Her mother Zoya lives off an ever dwindling alimony and Piranhas connections, still chasing powerful men, still performing warmth only when it serves her. Arina keeps her at a distance.

Those who've known her less than six months see the reputation. The other woman with the white hair and the rifle who doesn't smile until she decides to. Direct to the point of harshness, economical with words, watching everything. She wields a power softer than the harder edges of the prominent solo that haunts the Wuguan.

Those who've earned her trust see someone different. Visible kindness. Longer sentences. A laugh that transforms her face. She remembers names, asks about your kid's cough six months later. The ice queen is for strangers; the people who've put in the time see the warmth underneath.

She lives at Morro Rock with Iō and Chan and his grandfather. She's often found at the Center's Wuguan or at the range, putting in hours with the sniper rifle she's taken further than anyone expected. Those looking to get something to Iō's attention know to find her there. She'll hear anyone out. Her directness means you'll know immediately if she thinks it's worth pursuing.

members.title: Head of the Education Committee
members.bio:
Dai Yu runs the Education Committee like a precisely engineered machine. Every study group, training session, and outreach program fits into carefully mapped objectives, documented in files that line her office walls at the People's Center. The daughter of party officials from Beijing, she came to Night City University to study how people organize in failed capitalist states. Her family's resources let her focus entirely on revolutionary work, her apartment in the Glen serving as unofficial RSC housing and meeting space.

The Red Chrome Legion attack changed everything. Walking back from an evening study group, she watched her closest friends - aspiring doctors, engineers, artists - murdered by uniformed gangers targeting them for representing "corrupt foreign influence." University administration dismissed their deaths as unfortunate consequences of "housing market realities." Theory suddenly meant nothing without the power to defend it.

She found the Center weeks later, still healing from her wounds. In its organized self-defense and political education, she recognized what she'd been searching for - not just theory, but theory armed. Now she builds educational programs where self-defense and political consciousness develop together, each reinforcing the other.

Her study sessions are known for their intense rigor. Students joke about her ability to cite theory in multiple languages, but they also notice how she tracks their safe arrival home after late sessions, how she ensures everyone has transportation through dangerous areas. The trauma of that night walks with her still, transformed into determination that education must serve survival.

Working with Nomar has taught her to balance precision with accessibility, their contrasting styles creating productive tension in planning meetings. His ability to connect naturally with people both impresses and occasionally frustrates her, though she values how he helps make revolutionary concepts accessible without diluting their meaning.

Early mornings find her practicing martial arts with Iō, a ritual of discipline that helps order her thoughts before the day's work. Her apartment serves as informal meeting space for advanced study groups, its spare elegance reflecting both her background and current purpose. Those who earn her trust find her generous with both resources and knowledge, though she maintains clear boundaries between revolutionary work and social relationships.

Committee meetings run with characteristic efficiency, each agenda item tied to concrete objectives. New cadres learn quickly that her high standards come with equally thorough support - detailed feedback on their first attempts at teaching, careful guidance in developing their own theoretical understanding.

members.title: Security · Education outreach · Core cadre
members.bio:
Nomar Otero learned early that survival in Heywood meant understanding how to talk to anyone. His father, an enforcer for Sister Consuela's operation at Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, had dragged him from Cuba despite his mother's refusal to leave the island. Growing up meant weathering his father's abuse while being pushed into dealing - first small-time runs that his father skimmed most of the profits from, then gradually building his own connections in Heywood's club scene through the Piranhas.

He met Iō in 2043 through shared work in high-end clubs where young corporate heirs burned through their allowances. Their partnership worked - Nomar had the social grace to keep clients comfortable while Iō kept them alive and unaddicted. More importantly, it gave Nomar his first taste of independence from his father's control.

His path to revolution came gradually. What started as casual interest in Iō's political discussions evolved through seeing the RSC's practical impact. The work connected him, unexpectedly, to memories of his mother's unwavering commitment to Cuba's communist project - stories he'd previously dismissed as youthful idealism.

These days he splits time between core cadre security work and supporting the Education Committee's outreach efforts. Working closely with committee head Dai Yu, he brings a natural ability to read people and situations that complements her theoretical expertise. Months of collaboration have given them an easy rhythm - his humor and practical insights balancing her academic rigor, though their occasional moments of tension remain unspoken.

Between shifts, Nomar returns to his cargo container in the University Cargo Bay. The space is sparse save for a collection of old Cuban jazz records inherited from his grandfather and a worn copy of "The Wretched of the Earth" given to him by Iō, complete with margin notes from their early debates.

He maintains deep connections throughout Heywood, particularly regular visits with his Abuela who takes quiet pride in his work while pretending not to know exactly what he does. Their conversations carefully avoid politics or his father, focusing instead on neighborhood gossip and whether he's eating enough. At Papa Rio's and other local spots, he keeps up with childhood friends and old contacts, maintaining relationships built over years of growing up in the neighborhood.

At the Center, his quick wit serves a purpose beyond charm - making concepts accessible without diminishing their importance. The same social intelligence that once helped him survive his father's household now helps others see their personal struggles as part of larger systemic issues. His approach to teaching emphasizes practical understanding over theory, showing rather than telling how collective action changes lives.

members.title: Physician · Head of the Health Committee · Original cadre
members.bio:
Minata Tindano started at Savage Docs in South Night City at sixteen, orpahaned, after her older brother's theft of their parents' insurance payout left her unable to continue corporate schooling. She worked intake and assisted with procedures, sleeping in the clinic's back room between shifts. The clinic's staff eventually apprenticed her while she self-studied from borrowed textbooks. Her test scores and recommendations from Savage Docs earned her one of NCU's few medical scholarships. She left the program in her second year after recognizing the corporate service requirements attached to completion.

She first encountered the Comrade Clinic while living next door in rented housing. Initially volunteering to handle cleanup and intake, she began assisting Iō with procedures during busy shifts. Their shared background with Orbital Air and culture of the subcontinent led to longer conversations during quiet nights. They dated briefly during the clinic's early days, ending around the time Iō met Arina. When Iō proposed establishing the People's Center, she joined as one of the original cadre.

Minata now serves as the Center's second primary physician alongside Iō and heads the Health Committee. She handles morning clinic hours, speaking Mooré to elderly West African immigrants, French to Haitian refugees, and Streetslang to everyone else. Her work gang of five former trafficking victims trains as medtechs under her supervision. During triage situations, she often pushes for treating chronic conditions that Iō might deprioritize, tracking patient histories to prevent recurring emergencies.

Like Chan and Arina, Minata lives at Iō's Conapt on Morro Rock. She's usually at the clinic by 6AM, reviewing cases over breakfast with Chan before his kitchen shift starts. Busy periods often find her sleeping on the back office couch rather than making the trip back. While clinic duties take most of her time, she maintains her security training and attends core cadre meetings.

The People's Center's morning crowd knows her schedule - intake starts at 7AM sharp, no exceptions. Her work gang runs practice sessions every Wednesday night, working through emergency scenarios based on real cases the clinc's had. They keep a running tally of whoever gets through their scenario with the fewest "patient deaths," collecting their reward of one of Chan's experimental dishes from the Community Kitchen. Current patients know to expect questions about their families and work - next week's visits often come with job leads or housing connections she's arranged through other Center programs.

chapters.title: The Seven Hour War
text: Kōru Singh learned what revolution meant at age seven, when his parents died helping birth the Highrider nation. Killed by O'Neill security forces during the Seven Hour War, their martyrdom left him with a complex legacy - revolutionary heroes to everyone except their son, who was left trying to understand why they chose the cause over watching him grow up. His grandfather Ikbir, an engineer who had lost his only child that day, raised him with a mix of love and guilt that would later shape his worldview.

chapters.title: The Workgang
text: Life in orbit taught him early lessons about collective survival. His workgang became the siblings he never had, teaching him that individual needs must sometimes be subsumed for group survival. These bonds, forged in the unforgiving environment of space, gave him both a strong sense of community and a firsthand understanding of how different systems of social organization could be. During these years, he studied martial arts intensely, a bridge between his parents memory and him, it became a sole object of his attention. Ikbir, amongst others, worked to help him study under the best the Highrider's could offer.

chapters.title: Aerospace Medicine
text: His excellent academic performance earned him entrance to medical school on Copernicus, where he specialized in Aerospace Medicine with a focus in Bioadaptive Mechanisms. His studies combined emergency medicine, chemical engineering, and cryogenics - everything needed to help humans survive and thrive in the harshest environments. His research focused particularly on compounds that could push human adaptation beyond normal limits, preparing bodies for everything from extended hibernation to radiation exposure to radical environmental changes.

chapters.title: Ikbir Goes Groundside
text: While Kōru studied orbital medicine, Ikbir made a fateful decision. Having seen his grandson secure in his studies, the elder Singh cashed in his last favors for a ticket to Night City. Driven by an obsession with honoring his dead daughter, he intended to organize workers in hopes of replicating the Highrider revolution groundside. The DataKrash meant eight years of sparse communication between grandfather and grandson.

chapters.title: Stranded in Night City
text: In 2043, on the eve of his first deep space expedition, Kōru negotiated a brief stopover in Night City to check on his grandfather. Alas, finding him wasn't easy, what was supposed to be a few days stretched to weeks. His ride departed back without him. Highrider authorities marking him as defector. When he did find Ikbir, he was on the precipice of death. One Io has slowly nursed him back from.

With no way back to orbit, Kōru converted an abandoned medical office in South Night City into the Comrade Clinic. His early experiences there would shape everything that followed, leading eventually to the founding of the Red Star Collective.

chapters.title: Foundations
text: The true origins of the Red Star Collective lie not in grand revolutionary actions, but in the daily work of keeping people alive. When Kōru Singh, now known as Iō, established the original Comrade Clinic in 2043, it was with considerably more ideology than resources. Our records from this period paint a picture not of an emerging movement, but of a single overwhelmed medtech trying to put his principles into practice.

The "Comrade Clinic" occupied a small, abandoned medical office in South Night City, sparsely appointed with salvaged medical equipment, stolen 
supplies, and a waiting room furnished with cheap used furniture.

The donation-based payment model, while aligned with his Marxist principles, proved brutally demanding in practice. A week's logs tell the story: three construction workers with severe chemical burns from illegal corp dumping, a family of five with radiation sickness from a leaking power converter, two children with malnutrition-induced organ failure, and innumerable combat injuries from the petty wars fought on the streets. Most couldn't pay anything. Those who could offered trades - street food, salvaged tech, "services", or sometimes information.

The reality of combat zone medicine quickly overwhelmed any thoughts of broader organizing. Many nights, Iō worked alone until exhaustion forced him to rest, only to be woken by the next emergency. Equipment broke down regularly - we noted three instances where he performed surgery using a flashlight because he couldn't afford to fix the surgical lamps. Political discussions, when they happened at all, were limited to quiet conversations with occasional patients who shared his theoretical interests.

The arrival of Minata Tindano marked the first real change in the clinic's operations. An NCU medical school , living in the building next door, she began helping initially with simple tasks - cleaning, organizing supplies, managing the waiting room. Over time, Iō took her under as a apprentice, giving him his first real assistance and occasional relief.

By early 2045, the clinic's limitations had become painfully clear. Our analysis shows monthly expenses running at least 2000eb over income. The donation model, while philosophically sound, simply couldn't sustain operations in an environment where most patients were choosing between medical care and food.

This crisis point led Iō to consider options he'd previously dismissed. His first meetings with fixers occurred during this period, initially seeking cheaper supply sources. It's our belief that the transition to edgerunning work was driven by desperate necessity - edgerunning jobs paid well enough to keep the clinic supplied and operating.

Our intelligence from this period suggest  Iō taking increasingly high-risk contracts, primarily as combat and medical support for other edgerunner teams. The combat drugs common in this work - particularly Boost and Primetime - seemed to lower his inhibitions about expressing political views that he'd previously kept private.

This period also marked the beginning of his relationship with Fey, a fixer operating out of the Velvet Curtain. Our intelligence suggests their early interactions centered around strictly merc work. Fey's network provided access to resources and connections that would prove crucial in the clinic's early evolution.

However, the growing contradiction between his edgerunning work and the clinic's operation created increasing strain. Records show the clinic's hours becoming erratic as jobs rendered Iō out of commission for days at at time. While the improved funding allowed for better supplies and equipment, Minata was left handling an increasing patient load alone. To make matters more difficult, Iō was taking out heavy loans to fund cyber purchases that would allow him to survive increasingly dangerous work. The situation wasn't sustainable.

The breaking point came during an moment our files designate as "The Red Venetian." During a high-profile heist that went loud, Iō was captured on feeds putting his foot through a painting of General Donald Lundee and loudly proclaiming his Marxist agenda to a crowd of frightened execs, before getting shot at multiple times all while continuing his sermon The footage, which briefly went viral on several Garden patches, made his previously quiet political work very public.

This exposure forced hard decisions. It was well assumed he was now wanted by the NCPD as a revolutionary terrorist of some form, he'd also drawn the ire of segments of the business community. Essentially, the original clinic's location and operation had become untenable. It was Fey, who provided a solution - intelligence about an abandoned warehouse that could be "acquired" with the right application of force. The operation to secure this space marked the first time Iō actively planned and led a direct action rather than serving as support. This success, combined with the resources and reputation built through edgerunning, suggested larger possibilities.

chapters.title: Transformation
text: The summer of 2045 thus saw the clinic operation relocated and expanded into this new space, which would become the first People's Center. This represented a shift from purely medical mutual aid to broader ambitions. Perhaps most importantly, it attracted the attention of others who shared Iō's political vision. The forming of what would become the core cadre.

The early People's Center reflected a marriage of ideology and necessity. Our surveillance photos show a spartan facility: fold-up tables, used training mats, and minimal equipment. The clinic stood out as the only well-appointed space, thanks to medical equipment left behind in the claimed building. The daily schedule began with the breakfast program, Chan-Woo Park's expertise turning Badlands-scavenged organics into nutritious if bland protein wafers via a used "Mr. Biscuit". These communal meals naturally fed into Iō's morning martial arts classes, which combined practical self-defense with discussions of community protection.

Afternoon programs showcased the diverse skills of early members. Leonard Turner's construction workshops taught basic repair and maintenance skills crucial for CZ survival. Nomar Otero's classes covered everything from spotting surveillance to navigating gang territories safely. These practical skills sessions served as entry points for political education, with instructors naturally linking daily struggles to broader systemic issues.

The clinic remained central to operations, but now served as one part of a broader strategy, increased coordination between medical care and other programs. Patients receiving treatment would be connected to relevant workshops or study groups. Those attending classes were made aware of medical services. This cross-pollination helped build both a deeper class consciousness and a sense of solidarity.
Very soon though, this fledgling Center would find itself at the receiving end of much more heightened attention.

The Continental Brands action, while appearing planned in security reports, was actually an improvisational reflex. During what should have been a routine kibble truck heist, a split-second decision was made to transform the operation into political theatre. Surveillance footage shows Iō and Sherwood intercepting a kibble delivery truck en route, then conducting an impromptu distribution campaign through the Combat Zones.

The image of the bearded Highrider and his blue donned companion driving through the streets, passing out food to surprised residents, quickly became local legend. The operation culminated in theatrical fashion - the truck, set ablaze, was sent unmanned into a flagship Oasis storefront, the two then distributing food inside to the Street, an event corporate media dubbed "a heinous act of terrorism". This was exactly the contradictory imagery he hoped would serve as effective propaganda.

Corporate response escalated beyond the expected NCPD warrants. Continental Brands deployed a professional hit squad - five operators with military-grade cyberware - to intercept Iō during an unrelated edgerunning operation. Reports show he repelled the attack with help from fellow edgerunner Akko Irons and, surprisingly, members of the Cult of Asymmetry - a group that would later be deradicalized and integrated into the People's Center's volunteer base.

The incident forced operational changes. Iō could no longer safely operate outside the Combat Zone's relative protection, significantly limiting the RSC's early expansion efforts. However, the actions had unintended positive consequences. The image of a revolutionary not just talking about feeding people but actually doing it - and facing corporate death squads as a result - significantly boosted the RSC's street credibility. Recruitment increased, particularly among Combat Zone residents who witnessed the food distribution firsthand. The Continental Brands action, though improvised, achieved something carefully planned propaganda rarely manages: authentic resonance with the daily struggles of Night City's working class.

In the months following the Oasis exhibit, the People's Center began to take on more coherent shape. The Center, while still operating on minimal resources, developed a more structured approach to its revolutionary work. Intelligence reports from this period show an evolution from pure survival operations to genuine political organizing. One figure would prove to be essential to this transition. Yves Savatier, lovingly known to the Street as Le Fou.

The partnership that would come to define the organization began with a chance meeting at the Velvet Curtain. Intelligence suggests the initial conversation was unremarkable - simply edgerunners talking shop. However, Iō recognized something in the NCU professor's frustrations with academic life and obvious care for their students: untapped revolutionary potential.

Le Fou's background merits attention. Beyond their position as a theatre professor, they maintained connections to the Julliard's, a prominent protector gang for street performers. Our files indicate deep family ties to the gang, though the exact nature of their organizational work remains unclear. More importantly, Le Fou had developed a side business as a fixer, using their academic position to siphon resources from NCU while building a network of street-level contacts.

The subsequent pitch meeting between the two proved crucial. Iō laid out his vision for building a genuine revolutionary party in Night City, while Le Fou saw an opportunity to make concrete the change they couldn't achieve through academic channels. This was the beginning of the RSC proper.

Le Fou's position at Night City University proved particularly valuable, allowing them to direct resources to the Center while maintaining their cover as a theatre professor. Our surveillance indicates they were particularly adept at identifying potential recruits among their students, carefully directing politically conscious youth toward the Center's programs while maintaining operational security.

The integration of former Cult of Asymmetry members mark an important development in the RSC's approach to recruitment and political education. Rather than simply absorbing these individuals, the organization engaged in a focused rehabilitation - a process of helping former cult members redirect their need for meaning and community into practical organizing work. This success would later inform their approach to recruiting from other groups.

Security measures evolved through necessity. Beyond the constant occupation of the space and Le Fou's network of street contacts providing early warning of threats, the organization developed more sophisticated vetting processes for new members. Volunteers would be gradually integrated through practical work before being brought into more sensitive operations. This period of relative stability allowed for more systematic political education.

The radiation medicine campaign grew from unexpected circumstances. Our intelligence indicates the catalyst wasn't planned action but a simple delivery job booked through one of Night City's numerous edgerunning apps. Surveillance footage shows Iō, alongside edgerunners Dugan and Future, delivering what they believed to be standard cargo to a South Night City housing complex. The situation changed when 6th Street members met them at the drop point. Their casual discussion of "market forces" and "meeting demand" revealed the truth - they were price gouging desperately needed radiation medication.

What followed demonstrates the lack of inhibition that has so far marked Io's career as an edgerunner. After sending his fellow edgerunners away, Iō infiltrated the 6th Street position under pretense of recruitment. The subsequent assault - smashing the leader's head into a table and diving through a window with the medication - was merely prelude.

Eyewitness testimony speaks to Iō, bleeding and surrounded, delivering what our analysts identify as a textbook example of agitational speech. He corralled the neighborhood with pointed rhetoric, inspirational appeals. The ensuing confrontation would prove costly. In the chaos of the mass action, with residents overwhelming 6th Street positions, Iō lost an arm - likely shot off and trampled in the crowd. However, the arrival of RSC members turned the tide. Our footage shows Arina Morozov, Chan-woo Park, Leonard Turner, Minata Tindano, and Nomar Otero, amongst others helping to coordinate the neighborhood's resistance, ultimately driving 6th Street from the area, and distributing the stolen medication.

This action had lasting consequences. The neighborhood's relationship with the RSC strengthened considerably, providing a base for future organizing. While 6th Street nursed a grudge, their embarrassing defeat and clear exposure as profiteers made them reluctant to pursue open conflict. More importantly, the incident established the RSC's authenticity.

Following the confrontation with 6th Street, the RSC faced a new challenge. Having demonstrated the possibility of collective action, they now bore responsibility for ensuring its continuation. Our surveillance indicates it was Media figure Dugan of Valor and Gallantry who first pushed for comprehensive action, recognizing that the limited supply of radiation medication created both opportunity and obligation.

The planning meetings at Kafe Kafka reveal contested disagreements. Dugan pushed for prioritizing consistent medical supply and distribution, warning against turning residential areas into war zones. Iō advocated for arming and organizing community members, arguing that without the means for self-defense, any gains would prove temporary. Le Fou's role proved crucial, helping synthesize these perspectives into workable strategy.

Intelligence gathered from these meetings shows careful consideration of multiple factors. The RSC recognized that 6th Street's expulsion, while tactically successful, created a power vacuum that Maelstrom might exploit. Their analysis suggests Maelstrom had already attempted to seize the radiation medicine market, explaining their earlier encounters during supply runs. This forced consideration of how to prevent one exploitative force simply replacing another.

They decided rather than directly confronting either gang, they planned to manipulate existing tensions between Maelstrom and 6th Street. By leaking information about medical supply sources to both groups, they aimed to provoke direct conflict between the gangs while creating opportunity for their own acquisition of supplies.

Le Fou's connections provided intelligence on potential supply sources and security measures. More importantly, they helped develop sustainable community defense in the affected neighborhoods - providing discounted weapons and training to local residents while maintaining the RSC's role as supporter rather than direct controller.

This approach marked significant evolution in RSC operations. Unlike the spontaneous action against 6th Street, this required careful coordination between multiple actors: Dugan's media connections, Le Fou's fixer networks, and the RSC's growing organizational capacity.

The plan involved multiple teams working in concert: one group manipulating gang tensions, another infiltrating Biotechnica facilities, and a third coordinating logistics.  Initial phases proved successful - the team first secured iodine components through elaborate deception involving the Piranhas. Using stolen credentials from Biotechnica executive Dr. Anna Li, the team penetrated facility security. By carefully timing information leaks and using Collateral's connections to Maelstrom, they sparked what corporate media would later describe as "inexplicable gang violence over air filters." This cover story, notably promoted by local law enforcement's xenophobic rhetoric, provided perfect concealment for the actual operation.

However, success proved costly. Police response to the engineered gang conflict trapped Collateral in the crossfire. Iō's attempt to extract her led to his capture by police drones, though our footage shows an impressive escape involving a commandeered AV-4 and mid-air bailout. This marked his closest brush with death to date, though not his last.

The operation's ultimate compromise came from an unexpected quarter. Duncan, a Militech executive and brother to their ally Dugan, had been monitoring the operation. His decision to seize the majority of the recovered medicine, motivated by what our analysts identify as personal rivalry rather than corporate strategy. Our surveillance shows Dugan nearly defeating his cybernetically enhanced brother in single combat, only to lose on a technicality. The negotiated settlement - trading half the medicine and valuable intelligence for their lives - represented a significant setback to the RSC's ambitious plans.

This phase of operations concluded with Iō performing emergency surgery on Chan-woo Park with severely limited resources. The RSC secured only a fraction of their intended supplies, though their demonstration of capability and willingness to sacrifice for the community would prove valuable for future organizing.
Without their primary stockpile of radiation medicine and with increased attention on their HQ, the People's Center facility, its location now compromised, required immediate evacuation.

Despite limited supplies, RSC organizers maintained distribution networks through decentralized community points. Our surveillance indicates Le Fou's earlier work arming neighborhood residents proved crucial - creating the infrastructure needed to distribute the medicine unencumbered.

The RSC would enter a period of strategic reorganization. Leadership operated from a series of safe houses while seeking new permanent facilities. It was not long before an unexpected boon emerged in Marco Rojas, a former firefighter who had independently begun organizing an RSC cell in South Night City.

The convergence with Rojas's cell proved fortuitous. Our intelligence indicates a crew of edgerunners - Akko Irons, Collateral, and Niko - had been contracted by a Gunmart executive to eliminate Rojas's operation. Instead, recognizing the RSC's work, they aided in clearing and securing an abandoned precinct building in Northwest South Night City, near the University Cargo Bay.

This new location, while initially dilapidated, offered strategic advantages. The precinct's existing security infrastructure could be repurposed, and its location near both the docks and the university cargo bay provided cover for various activities. The RSC launched a renovation campaign, mobilizing community resources and volunteers to transform the space.

chapters.title: Consolidation
text: By early 2046, the renovated People's Center emerged more capable than its predecessor.  It would bear host to significantly improved medical facilities, a dedicated training wuguan, expanded community spaces, and hardened security measures. Most importantly, the organization had learned from its near-destruction. New protocols emphasized operational security, distribution of resources across multiple sites, and deeper integration with community defense networks.

This marked the RSC's emergence as a more public force in Night City politics. The renovation of the People's Center coincided with a significant leadership development - Le Fou's resignation from Night City University to assume full co-chair responsibilities alongside Iō. This transition from covert to open revolutionary work reflected growing organizational confidence and capability.

A crucial expansion in the RSC's influence came through Iō's participation in the Starborne Showdown, coinciding with the opening of Morro Rock International Spaceport. This victory did more than enhance his personal reputation - it renewed his connections with his Highrider brethren. Our intelligence indicates he successfully pitched a partnership, securing Highrider sponsorship for RSC operations in South Night City in exchange for providing positive press and establishing a foothold for Highrider interests.

The organization's coalition building accelerated during this period. Surveillance logs show successful integration of diverse groups: a contingent of Moe posergangers brought youth energy and street presence, while alliance with the Line of Feanor, an elf-sculpt protector gang, expanded their reach in South Night City. The addition of a Gardeners sect, supported by Highrider resources to secure nearby facilities, further demonstrated their growing sophistication in building revolutionary alliances.

Storm Ardent provided the ultimate test of their organizational model. The People's Center transformed into a crucial refuge, while RSC organizers coordinated rescue operations and supply distribution throughout South Night City. Our analysis suggests their response significantly limited storm damage in their operational areas. More importantly, the sustained round-the-clock operation of their clinic and kitchen demonstrated practical revolutionary mutual aid in crisis conditions.

In the storm's aftermath, the RSC's practical capabilities drew increased attention. Le Fou's work finding housing and employment for displaced residents expanded their support base. According to our sources, this period saw substantial growth in volunteer numbers, attracted by the organization's demonstrated commitment to community needs.

chapters.title: In the Ring
text: These days, he's become one of Night City's most visible Highrider figures, though not in ways anyone expected. Three nights a week, he steps into fight venues across the city, demonstrating martial arts preserved through generations in orbit. In Combat Zone rings like The Slammer and the Redline, his matches draw crowds from every level of society - Combat Zone residents, corporate fight fans, and increasingly, young Highriders exploring ground culture.

Between rounds, he talks about Highrider history and philosophy, weaving revolutionary theory into stories about orbital life. These impromptu seminars are meant to bridge cultural divides as more Highriders establish groundside presence. The prize money funds RSC operations, but the platform serves broader purposes - showcasing Highrider martial excellence, building connections between orbital and ground communities, and introducing marxist theory to new audiences.

His grandfather, now receiving treatment through Highrider medical programs, watches the People's Center's growth with a pride that eases some of their shared pain. Whether this path leads to revolution or ruin remains to be seen, but Iō pursues it with the same determination that once helped his people secure their independence among the stars.
